metadata.description: Cross-framework compliance mapping rules for Neomnix GRC. Maps technical findings from Nmap, OWASP ZAP, and SharkTap passive analysis to regulatory controls.

mappings.description: Cleartext database traffic detected. HIPAA mandates encryption of PHI in transit. SOC2 CC6.7 requires secure data transmission.
Unencrypted database traffic observed via passive network tap. Database connections must be encrypted to protect sensitive data in transit.

mappings.technical_trigger: Active Port Scan Detected from Internal Host
mappings.description: An internal host is actively scanning ports — potential reconnaissance or compromised machine. HIPAA requires risk analysis and incident response. SEC rules may require disclosure of material cybersecurity events.

mappings.technical_trigger: DNS Tunneling Suspected — Potential Data Exfiltration
mappings.description: Suspiciously long DNS queries suggest DNS tunneling — a technique used to exfiltrate data by encoding it in DNS query names. This is a high-confidence indicator of a security incident requiring immediate investigation and potential SEC disclosure.

mappings.technical_trigger: Unencrypted Credential Transmission via HTTP POST
mappings.description: HTTP POST requests captured in plaintext — credentials or sensitive data may be exposed. All authentication must occur over encrypted channels (HTTPS/TLS 1.2+).
Active Telnet sessions observed. Telnet transmits all data including credentials in cleartext. Must be replaced with SSH. Critical HIPAA violation for any environment handling PHI.

mappings.technical_trigger: Cleartext File Transfer Protocol (FTP) Session Detected
mappings.description: FTP sessions transmit file contents and credentials in plaintext. Replace with SFTP (SSH File Transfer) or FTPS (FTP over TLS).

mappings.technical_trigger: Large Outbound Data Transfer — Possible Exfiltration
mappings.description: Unusually large outbound data transfers detected. May indicate data exfiltration or unauthorized bulk data movement. Requires investigation.
Exposure of sensitive information via insecure FTP proxy.
SQL Injection vulnerability allows attacker to read, modify, or delete database contents including PHI. Critical HIPAA and SEC cybersecurity risk.
Reflected XSS allows injection of malicious scripts into web pages. Can be used to steal session tokens or redirect users.
Telnet port open. Use of cleartext Telnet for remote administration. Must be replaced with SSH immediately.
FTP port open. Cleartext file transfer protocol. Replace with SFTP or FTPS.
Service protected by TCP wrapper but still exposed externally. May permit unauthorized connection attempts.
Server directory listing enabled. Exposes internal file structure.
Path traversal allows access to files outside the web root. Can expose configuration files containing credentials.
HTTP on port 80. Unencrypted web service. Must redirect to HTTPS. Any transmission of PHI over HTTP violates HIPAA.
Weak TLS protocol (SSLv3, TLS 1.0, or TLS 1.1) detected. HIPAA requires current encryption standards. Upgrade to TLS 1.2+ minimum.

mappings.technical_trigger: ZAP Alert: Server Side Request Forgery
mappings.description: SSRF allows the server to make requests to internal resources. Can be used to probe internal services or access cloud metadata endpoints.
Remote code execution vulnerability. Complete system compromise possible. Immediate incident response required. Likely SEC material cybersecurity incident.
